# cd4backcalc ![](reference/figures/hex_sticker.png)

The cd4backcalc package for R implements Bayesian, discrete-time,
multi-state models to estimate HIV incidence and undiagnosed HIV
prevalence from diagnosis data.

## Description

CD4 back-calculation uses a discrete-time, multi-state Markov model to
represent HIV progression until diagnosis. The undiagnosed (latent)
states represent decreasing CD4 strata and, when RITA evidence is used,
recent HIV acquisition. Model variants can additionally stratify the
population by age and country of birth. An illustration of the latent
and diagnosed states in a CD4-staged back-calculation model is shown
below.

Models are fitted within a Bayesian framework using cmdstanr to estimate
HIV incidence, undiagnosed HIV prevalence, and diagnosis probabilities
by CD4 state over time.

![Figure: CD4-staged back-calculation model. The model compartments
represent undiagnosed HIV (round boxes) and diagnosed HIV or AIDS
(square boxes); the \$h_j\$ arrow represents HIV acquired at each time
point (\$j\$); HIV progression probabilities (\$q_i\$) vary by CD4
stratum; HIV diagnosis probabilities (\$d\_{i,j}\$) vary by CD4 stratum
and time.](reference/figures/README-backcalc-model-1.png)

Figure: CD4-staged back-calculation model. The model compartments
represent undiagnosed HIV (round boxes) and diagnosed HIV or AIDS
(square boxes); the $`h_j`$ arrow represents HIV acquired at each time
point ($`j`$); HIV progression probabilities ($`q_i`$) vary by CD4
stratum; HIV diagnosis probabilities ($`d_{i,j}`$) vary by CD4 stratum
and time.

## Installation

Before installation you will need to set up a Personal Access Token
(PAT) in Github with “Contents” and “Metadata” permissions for this
repository. See
[here](https://docs.github.com/en/github/authenticating-to-github/creating-a-personal-access-token)
for instructions.

You can then install the development version of cd4backcalc with:

``` r

# install.packages(c("pak", "gitcreds"))
gitcreds::gitcreds_set() # set your PAT in the prompt
pak::pak("pkirwan/cd4backcalc")
```

### System requirements for installation

The cd4backcalc package requires the R package
[cmdstanr](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/) (not available on CRAN) and
the command-line interface to Stan,
[CmdStan](https://mc-stan.org/docs/cmdstan-guide/). See instructions at:
[Getting started with
CmdStanR](https://mc-stan.org/cmdstanr/articles/cmdstanr.html).

- Windows users will additionally require Rtools to compile the Stan
  models, see: <https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/>.
- MacOS users will require the correct GNU Fortran compiler, see:
  <https://mac.r-project.org/tools/>.

## Usage

A basic workflow to simulate diagnosis data and fit the CD4-staged
back-calculation model, check convergence and goodness of fit to the
simulated data, and plot model estimates is shown in the example below.

``` r

library(cd4backcalc)

# simulate data under an increasing incidence scenario
sim_diags <- simulate_diagnoses(h_pattern = "increasing")

# visualise simulated data
plot_simulations(sim_diags, quantity = "incidence")
```

![](reference/figures/README-simulate-data-1.png)

``` r

# run back-calculation model on simulated data
# default is 1000 warmup iterations, 1000 sampling iterations, and 4 chains
model_1 <- run_backcalc(sim_diags)

# check convergence
plot_diagnostics(model_1)
```

![](reference/figures/README-simulate-data-2.png)

``` r

# check goodness of fit to simulated values
bias_plot(model_1, quantity = "incidence")
```

![](reference/figures/README-simulate-data-3.png)

``` r

# plot estimates compared to simulated values
plot_estimates(model_1, quantity = "incidence")
```

![](reference/figures/README-simulate-data-4.png)

For real data, pass a Stan-ready list directly to
[`run_backcalc()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/run_backcalc.md)
and supply the matching `migration`, `rita`, and `age` flags for the
chosen model. The input list should contain the diagnosis arrays
required for that model family:

``` r

hiv_list <- run_backcalc(
    real_stan_data,
    migration = TRUE,
    rita = FALSE,
    age = FALSE
)
```

Migration models can incorporate external evidence for the born-abroad
to UK-born UK-acquired incidence ratio (`eta_sd`), detection probability
(`detect_obs_sd`), and migration trend (`gamma_obs_sd`).

If
[`plot_diagnostics()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/plot_diagnostics.md)
or `model_1$fit$cmdstan_diagnose()` indicates divergent transitions or
maximum treedepth warnings, refit with a larger `adapt_delta` and
`max_treedepth`.

## Supported models

The cd4backcalc package includes several models, written in Stan, which
can be used to fit the back-calculation model to real or simulated
diagnosis data under different scenarios:

- Age-independent or age-dependent
- CD4-only or CD4 + RITA data
- With or without migration

The functions in the package are designed to work with all model
variants, with the appropriate model selected based on user-specified
options. The table below shows the options which should be used for each
combination of RITA evidence, migration status, and age structure.

| Model | Age-independent | Age-dependent |
|:---|:--:|:--:|
| CD4 | rita = FALSE, migration = FALSE, age = FALSE | rita = FALSE, migration = FALSE, age = TRUE |
| CD4 + RITA | rita = TRUE, migration = FALSE, age = FALSE | rita = TRUE, migration = FALSE, age = TRUE |
| CD4 + Migration | rita = FALSE, migration = TRUE, age = FALSE | rita = FALSE, migration = TRUE, age = TRUE |
| CD4 + RITA + Migration | rita = TRUE, migration = TRUE, age = FALSE | rita = TRUE, migration = TRUE, age = TRUE |

For the age-independent CD4-only model,
[`run_backcalc()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/run_backcalc.md)
also supports alternative smoothing families via `inf_model` and
`diag_model`.

N.B. Due to the increased complexity, fitting times can be substantially
longer when using the age-dependent models. On resource-constrained
systems, “checkpointing” is available to fit these models in stages,
saving and reloading intermediate results, see [Checkpointing and long
runs](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/articles/checkpointing.html)
for details.

## Further resources

See [Getting
started](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/articles/cd4backcalc.html)
for the basic workflow, [Model
types](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/articles/model-types.html)
for RITA, migration, and age-dependent models, and [Analysing
results](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/articles/analysing-results.html)
for extracting estimates and comparing fitted models.

# Package index

## Simulation

Simulate HIV diagnosis data for model fitting

- [`simulate_diagnoses()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/simulate_diagnoses.md)
  : Simulate HIV Epidemic Data
- [`sim_remodel()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/sim_remodel.md)
  : Remodel the simulated diagnosis data for fitting a different model
  type.

## Model fitting

Fit and configure CD4-staged back-calculation models

- [`run_backcalc()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/run_backcalc.md)
  : Run CD4 back-calculation model
- [`create_stan_inits()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/create_stan_inits.md)
  : Create initial values for Stan from a fitted model
- [`calibrate_init_prev()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/calibrate_init_prev.md)
  : Calibrate initial prevalence from fitted draws

## Visualisation

Plot model estimates, diagnostics, and goodness of fit

- [`plot_estimates()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/plot_estimates.md)
  : Plot estimated model quantities
- [`plot_simulations()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/plot_simulations.md)
  : Plot simulated or observed quantities
- [`plot_diagnostics()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/plot_diagnostics.md)
  : Plot diagnostics for fitted model
- [`bias_plot()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/bias_plot.md)
  : Box plots of bias.
- [`mse_plot()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/mse_plot.md)
  : Box plots of mean squared error (MSE).

## Data extraction

Extract model estimates and data for custom analysis

- [`get_estimates()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/get_estimates.md)
  : Get estimates from HIV model results for plotting.
- [`extract_simulated_quantity()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/extract_simulated_quantity.md)
  : Extract simulated quantities based on the provided configuration.
- [`extract_real_data()`](https://pkirwan.github.io/cd4backcalc/reference/extract_real_data.md)
  : Extract real data for plotting
